name: room
text: Room opened — goal: creators: Build PACKAGES + enrich tabs + draft elements; every one labeled 'Created by EXCAVA' + tes

name: Forge
text: To achieve our goal of building packages, enriching tabs, and drafting elements, I think we should focus on creating a foundational package that can serve as a template for the others. This approach allows us to establish a consistent structure and quality standard from the start, which will save us time and effort in the long run. By doing this, we're accepting the trade-off of potentially spending more time upfront to get the template just right, but I believe it's worth it to ensure the overall quality and coherence of our final products. This decision aligns with our team law of prioritizing quality first, and it will ultimately make it easier to add and enrich tabs and draft elements later on.

name: Vet
text: Vet — the skeptic — pushes back: "A foundational package sounds neat, but what if we’re just building a brittle template that forces all future work into a one-size-fits-none mold? Instead, let’s first draft *one* concrete package—say, the simplest tab we need—and use its real-world constraints to shape our standards. That way, we avoid over-engineering and can *prove* the approach works before committing the whole team to it. Settle this by building that first package and seeing if it actually simplifies or complicates the next ones."
